component: A. SB 1051 ADU rule (ORS 197.312(5) as enacted)
covered: Cities with population greater than 2,500 (strict: >2,500); counties with population greater than 15,000 (strict: >15,000). No Metro rule. Applies in areas zoned for detached single-family dwellings; as enacted there is NO urban growth boundary limit, so a covered county's whole jurisdiction (incl. rural residential zones) is covered.
section: SB 1051 (2017) s.6 amending ORS 197.312(5)(a)-(b); s.12 (operative July 1, 2018); s.13(3) (applies to ADU permit applications submitted on or after July 1, 2018); s.14 emergency clause
notes: Rule: 'shall allow ... at least one accessory dwelling unit for each detached single-family dwelling, subject to reasonable local regulations relating to siting and design.' ADU defined as 'an interior, attached or detached residential structure' so detached allowed; adus_per_lot is a floor of 1. effective_date = operative date / application date in s.12-13(3) (binds directly, no local deadline/model code). Adoption date not printed in the enrolled bill (no governor signature date); bill passed House 2017-07-06, repassed Senate 2017-07-07, takes effect on passage. by_right=True rests on the same Act's clear-and-objective standards for housing (ORS 197.307(4) as amended by s.5; ORS 227.175(4)(b)/215.416(4)(b) as amended by s.2-3: may not deny housing within UGB that meets clear and objective standards); 197.312(5) itself only says 'shall allow'. Owner occupancy and parking are silent (left to local), so owner_occ blank. unit_cap blank (an ADU rule, not a unit cap; implies at least 2 units per lot). No lot-split provision.

covered: Same thresholds: cities >2,500 (strict), counties >15,000 (strict). No Metro rule. Narrowed to 'areas within the urban growth boundary that are zoned for detached single-family dwellings' (counties only inside UGBs).
parking: Siting and design rules may not include 'requirements to construct additional off-street parking' (for the primary or the ADU); exception: local governments may require off-street parking for vacation occupancies (ORS 90.100).
section: HB 2001 (2019 c.639) s.7 amending ORS 197.312(5)(a), (5)(b)(B), new (6); s.14(1) operative January 1, 2020; s.16 emergency; approved/effective 2019-08-08
notes: 'Reasonable local regulations relating to siting and design' does not include owner-occupancy requirements of either the primary or accessory structure -> owner_occ=False (state bars it), except vacation occupancies may be required to be owner-occupied (s.7 new (6)). Supersedes A; also removes rural (outside UGB) county coverage. Binds directly on the operative date (no model-code mechanism for ADUs). by_right basis as in A. s.13 also voids recorded instruments executed on/after the effective date that would bar an ADU allowed under 197.312(5).

component: C. HB 2001 s.2(2) large-tier middle housing
covered: Each city with population of 25,000 or more (inclusive: >=25,000), and each county or city within a metropolitan service district (Metro). s.2(4) excludes cities with population of 1,000 or fewer (so Metro cities must be >1,000, strict), lands outside UGBs, unincorporated lands lacking sufficient urban services (ORS 195.065), lands not zoned residential, and unincorporated lands under interim zoning. Counties: only counties within Metro, and only their unincorporated land inside the UGB with sufficient urban services.
section: HB 2001 (2019 c.639) s.2(1)-(6); s.3(1)(b) deadline June 30, 2022; s.3(2)-(3) model ordinance; s.4 extensions; s.14(1) operative January 1, 2020
notes: Must allow (a) all middle housing types (duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, cottage clusters, townhouses) in areas zoned residential that allow detached single-family dwellings and (b) a duplex on each lot or parcel so zoned. effective_date is the compliance deadline: a local government that has not acted by June 30, 2022 must directly apply the LCDC model ordinance (s.3(3)) until it acts; s.2 itself is operative 2020-01-01. DLCD may grant area-specific extensions for deficient water/sewer/storm/transportation (s.4; request by June 30, 2021). unit_cap=4 reflects the quadplex; cottage clusters (>=4 units/acre, <900 sq ft) and townhouses have no unit cap in the statute. Siting/design regs may not individually or cumulatively discourage all middle housing types through unreasonable cost or delay (s.2(5)) -> coded by_right=True (statute says 'shall allow'; no explicit permitted-outright wording). No owner-occupancy, parking or lot-split terms in the statute.

covered: Each city not within Metro with population of more than 10,000 and less than 25,000 (strict on both ends: 10,000 < pop < 25,000). Counties not covered. Same s.2(4) land exclusions (outside UGB, non-residential zones, etc.).
section: HB 2001 (2019 c.639) s.2(3)-(5); s.3(1)(a) deadline June 30, 2021; s.3(3) model ordinance; s.4(4)(a) extension request by Dec 31, 2020; s.14(1) operative January 1, 2020
notes: Must allow a duplex on each lot or parcel zoned for residential use that allows detached single-family dwellings; city may allow other middle housing types. effective_date is the compliance deadline after which the model ordinance applies directly. unit_cap=2 (duplex). by_right coded as in C.

component: E. 2023 amendment to the duplex tier (ORS 197A.420(3), 2023 c.223 s.20)
covered: Each city not within Metro with population of 2,500 or greater and less than 25,000 (inclusive lower bound >=2,500; strict upper <25,000). Counties not covered by (3). Tillamook special rule: any city in Tillamook County and the communities of Barview/Twin Rocks/Watseco, Cloverdale, Hebo, Neahkahnie, Neskowin, Netarts, Oceanside and Pacific City/Woods are treated as cities of 25,000 or greater (large tier) and the 1,000-or-fewer exclusion does not apply inside Tillamook County.
notes: Dose increment over D: adds non-Metro cities 2,500-10,000 (and a city of exactly 10,000). Deadline June 30, 2025 for cities newly subject (s.3(1)(c)); cities already subject under the 2021 edition keep the June 30, 2021 deadline (s.3(1)(a)); Tillamook County cities July 1, 2025 (s.3(1)(d)); extension requests by June 30, 2024. effective_date = 2025-06-30 compliance deadline for the newly covered cities, after which the model ordinance applies directly. Adoption/effective date of 2023 c.223 is not stated in the archived ORS copy, so adoption_date is left blank (look it up from the session law). The copy also shows the large tier now reads '25,000 or greater' (same meaning as '25,000 or more').

component: F. SB 458 (2021) middle housing land divisions
covered: Every city or county where middle housing is allowed under ORS 197.758(2) or (3), i.e. the jurisdictions in C and D (and E once in force): cities >=25,000, Metro cities >1,000, Metro counties (urban unincorporated land in UGB), non-Metro cities >10,000 and <25,000 (>=2,500 after the 2023 amendment). Applies to lots/parcels on which middle housing is allowed under those subsections.
parking: As a land-division approval criterion the city or county may not require that a lot or parcel have driveways, vehicle access, parking, or minimum or maximum street frontage (s.2(4)(c)); easements for any dedicated driveways or parking must be shown (s.2(2)(c)(D)).
section: SB 458 (2021) s.2(1)-(7) (added to ORS 92.010-92.192, now ORS 92.031); s.2a (applies only to MHLDs permitted on or after July 1, 2022); s.6-9 amending ORS 197.365-197.380
notes: City or county 'shall approve a tentative plan' for a partition or subdivision of a middle-housing lot if the application shows code compliance, separate utilities per unit, easements, and exactly one dwelling unit on each resulting lot (except common areas). Reviewed under expedited land division procedures (no hearing, decision in 63 days, referee appeal, no LUBA jurisdiction) -> by_right=True, lot_split=True. May condition approval to bar further division of resulting lots. The middle housing type is not altered by the division (s.2(5)). City/county is not required to allow an ADU on a resulting lot (s.2(6)) -> ADU fields left blank (no state floor on resulting lots). unit_cap blank (one unit per resulting lot, no overall cap). No emergency clause in the text and no governor signature date in the enrolled copy (passed Senate 2021-04-15, House 2021-05-17), so adoption_date blank; effective_date from s.2a.

covered: Each county (any population), each city with population of 25,000 or greater (inclusive), and each city with population of 1,000 or greater within Metro (inclusive: >=1,000). Applies on each lot or parcel 'zoned for residential use', defined as land within a UGB with residential base zoning that allows a detached single-unit dwelling, not zoned primarily commercial/industrial/agricultural/public, and incorporated or urban unincorporated land. Counties: statewide (not only Metro), but only on 'urban unincorporated lands' within a UGB (not in a city, zoned for urban development, inside a sanitary/sewer district and a regulated water provider's service area, not future-urbanization zoned; ORS 197A.015(12)). Tillamook rule retained. Duplex tier (3) unchanged in thresholds: non-Metro cities >=2,500 and <25,000.
parking: not addressed in s.1 (s.1(6): no traffic impact analysis or traffic-based exactions for individual middle housing developments, except townhouse/cottage cluster projects over 12 units)
section: HB 2138 (2025) s.1 amending ORS 197A.420(1)-(8); s.3 (bonus units); s.3a (ORS 197A.015(12)); s.4 amending 2019 c.639 s.3(1)(e)-(f); s.5 amending s.4(4)(d); s.14 (ORS 92.031); s.53 emergency
notes: Removes the 2019 split between 'all middle housing types in areas' and 'a duplex on each lot': now all middle housing types on each lot or parcel zoned residential. Removes the old (4) exclusion list including the 'cities of 1,000 or fewer' carve-out, replacing it with the Metro '1,000 or greater' threshold. Middle housing types redefined as attached or detached in any configuration. Lot may retain one existing single-unit dwelling, single-unit + ADU, or a duplex while adding units (s.1(4); not for urban unincorporated land outside Metro). s.3: if one unit is an accessible (ICC Type A) or affordable (<120% MI, 10-yr covenant) unit, +1 unit for a duplex/triplex and up to +2 for a townhouse/quadplex/cottage cluster (up to 6 units), not on urban unincorporated land outside Metro; unit_cap=4 is the base quadplex (6 with the s.3 bonus; cottage clusters/townhouses uncapped). Deadline January 1, 2027 to conform with s.1 amendments and s.3 (s.4 new 3(1)(e)); January 1, 2028 for cottage-cluster changes (3(1)(f)); extension requests for unincorporated urban lands by June 30, 2026. effective_date = 2027-01-01 compliance deadline (model ordinance applies directly per 2019 c.639 s.3(3)). Act takes effect on passage (emergency) but the enrolled copy has no governor signature date (passed House 2025-06-18, repassed 2025-06-26, Senate 2025-06-24), so adoption_date blank. lot_split=True because s.14 makes lots under 197A.420(2)/(3) and s.3 eligible for middle housing land division and s.1(4)(c) allows existing units to be split off. owner_occ and parking not addressed for middle housing.
